{{Quote|Human warrior that hunts monsters by bow.|Description}}
'''Hunter''' is a [[Final Fantasy Tactics Advance jobs|job]] in ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics Advance]]'' available to [[human|humes]]. They wield the almighty greatbows and use them most proficiently against monsters. Almost all of their abilities are centered around monster-fighting, with abilities like Sidewinder (which doubles the attack when used against monsters).

The Hunter has favorable [[stat growth]] and access to Ultima Shot, a powerful ability which triples attack power, making it an especially devastating job. Its counterpart is the [[Sniper (Tactics Advance)|Sniper]], a [[viera]] job.

== Appearance ==
Hunters are humes equipped with hunting and nature survival gear. They wear a tan cap, green undershirt, a pair of white shorts, brown boots and beige gloves. A yellow satchel is slung over their right shoulder and a knife is holstered in the Hunter's belt. Enemy Hunters have purple shirts instead of green.

The Hunter's artwork shows him with a knife, but in gameplay Hunters can only equip greatbows. In ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift]]'' the [[Hunter (Tactics A2)|Hunter]] job class may equip both, although all of their A-Abilities and passive abilities are learned from greatbows.

==Growth==
Hunters rival [[Fighter (Tactics Advance)|Fighters]] for the position of best Attack-oriented hume job. Like its predecessor, the [[Archer (Tactics Advance)|Archer]], Hunters have higher MP, Attack, Resistance and Speed than their sword-wielding counterpart, but have lower HP, Magic Power and Defense in return.

Oust's chance of success depends on the number of KOs the caster has been responsible for, and the percentage of HP the target has left.
:<math>MinHP\% = 50 - Number of Units Caster has KO'd</math>
:<math>HP\% = [Target's Max HP * MinHP\% / 100]</math>
:<math>Hit\% = [(HP\% - Target's HP) * 100 / HP\%]</math>

Aim: Vitals has a random effect:
*11/101: Inflict Berserk
*25/101: Inflict Disable
*35/101: Inflict Blind
*25/101: Inflict Immobilize
*5/101: Reduce Target to 1 HP

Capture's chance of success is equal to the following:
:<math>Hit\% = [25 * (Target's Max HP - Target's HP) / Target's Max HP]</math>
Capture automatically fails under certain conditions.

==Capture guide==
Capture is a complicated attack as there are a number of factors that need to be in place to make it functional. The player must get in a fight with a monster and steadily weaken it but not kill it. The Hunter's Hunting ability and the [[Paladin (Tactics Advance)|Paladin's]] Subdue ability can be used slowly weaken the monster.

If there is 0% chance of being captured, one can go through the following checklist:
*The monster cannot be at full health, or have at least 23/24 of it.
*The monster cannot be the last remaining enemy on the battlefield. The player can revive another enemy, preferably rendering it [[Sleep (status)|asleep]], [[Disable (status)|disabled]], or [[Stop (status)|stopped]].
*The following enemies cannot be captured: Undead (Zombies and Vampires), Tonberrykind (Ton- and Masterberries), Rockbeasts (Toughskins and Blade Biters), and Fairies (Sprite and Titania).
*Any monster with a Hero Medal cannot be captured.
*A previously captured monster of the same species must not already occupy the available slot in the Monster Bank.

The success rate of Capture is mediocre at best; the best success rate is 24%, and Concentrate, Turbo MP, status ailments (including [[Stop (status)|Stop]] and [[Sleep (status)|Sleep]]), and the facing do not affect it. The success rate is determined solely by the monster's remaining HP. For every 24th of max HP that was taken off the monster, 1% is added to the success rate. The only thing the player can do to aid in their capture is to either bring in more Hunters (or at least units with "Hunt" as the secondary A-Ability with Capture) or Haste the Hunter.

After capturing the monster, the player can [[Morpher#Information|raise it]].

== Gameplay ==
Even though many of the Hunter abilities revolve around monsters, the class is a strong ranged combatant. Wielding greatbows and Weapon Atk+, Hunters can deal great physical damage. [[Archer (Tactics Advance)|Archer]] abilities fit well with the Hunter since they provide some more support. Hunters are also commonly run with [[Blue Magic (Tactics Advance)|Blue Magic]] since their MP is high enough to actually use it to useful effect. Hunters are required for capturing monsters and training [[Morpher]]. Overall, Hunters are strong ranged units well-geared to eliminate other ranged enemies and make monster encounters easier to handle.

Enemy Hunters' monster-related techniques are not very useful, but their other skills remain potent. The player should close the distance quickly, but mages and other fragile units will need to be wary; Hunters have an easy time reaching even the clan's backline fighters. Physical tanks, like [[Paladin (Tactics Advance)|Paladins]] or [[Defender (Tactics Advance)|Defenders]], can withstand Hunter attacks better than almost anyone else. When [[Law system (Tactics Advance)|laws]] are in effect against bows or their abilities, Hunters become helpless.
